user.description: Set up the Hauswacht intrusion alarm. The alarm starts disarmed. Sirens are not controlled in this version.

init.title: Hauswacht options
init.description: {saved}Every change is saved as soon as you submit the form; you then return to the menu.

code.title: PIN rules
code.description:
Users with a PIN: {pin_users}.

**Master PIN:** a simple PIN without separate users, e.g. so voice assistants (Alexa) can only disarm with a PIN. It also appears in the user list as “Master-PIN”.

As soon as a PIN exists, the panel requires it to disarm. With “Allow dashboard buttons despite PIN”, the dashboard buttons “Disarm now” and “End alarm” keep working – only logged-in Home Assistant users can reach them anyway.

⚠️ **Important:** As soon as **one** PIN exists, the panel (and Alexa) require a PIN to disarm – **from everyone**. People without a PIN can then only disarm via dashboard buttons (if allowed under PIN rules) or the push button. So: give everyone a PIN (shared PIN allowed) or no one.

**Lock after wrong entries** (shared by panel, keypads, readers and Alexa): from the 3rd a system message, from the 5th locked for one minute, then twice as long each time, at most 15 minutes. While locked, even a correct PIN is rejected. Failed attempts expire 24 hours after the last one. Reset: correct entry, button “Reset failed attempts” in the test card (administrators) or restart.

zones.title: Sensor groups
zones.description:
{saved}A **sensor group** is a group of sensors that are always monitored together – for example:

- **Perimeter**: all door and window contacts (with their tamper sensors)
- **Inside** or **Basement**: motion and presence sensors

In the **profiles** you then choose which sensor groups are armed: "Home" = perimeter only, "Away" = perimeter and inside.

Every sensor belongs to **exactly one** sensor group. Hauswacht only monitors sensors that are in a sensor group.

zone_add.title: Add sensor group
zone_add.description:
Select all sensors that belong to this sensor group. Sensors: binary sensors, locks and covers. After saving, Hauswacht shows every sensor with its **type** (door, window, motion …) – change it there.

Each sensor can only be in **one** sensor group.

data_description.label: Handy for many sensors: put the label directly on the sensor entity (not the device); new sensors with the label then belong to the sensor group automatically.

zone_edit_settings.description:

Each sensor can only be in **one** sensor group.

infrastructure.title: Monitor radio networks and gateways
infrastructure.description:
Select sensors that report whether a radio network or gateway is running – e.g. the connection state of the Zigbee2MQTT bridge or an MQTT broker. If such a system fails, all sensors behind it can no longer report. Hauswacht reports the fault and treats arming as with unavailable sensors.

For sensors of type “problem”, “on” means fault; for all others “on” means OK.

homecoming.title: Homecoming observation
homecoming.description:
Hauswacht records when entry doors open and people are detected as home – per location source – and calculates whether automatic homecoming would be reliable. The observation switches NOTHING: no disarm, no alarm. Press “Homecoming report” for the report.

**Home Wi-Fi(s):** names of your Wi-Fi networks, comma separated (e.g. for the companion app's Wi-Fi sensor). In the next step you choose additional signals per person.

The observation also measures how long it takes from “door opened” to “disarmed” – which gives a recommendation for the entry delay.

users.title: Users and PINs
users.description:
{saved}Several people with their own PIN. Several users may share a PIN – Hauswacht then shows “shared PIN (…)”. An action is allowed if at least one user with that PIN may do it.

⚠️ **Important:** As soon as **one** PIN exists, the panel (and Alexa) require a PIN to disarm – **from everyone**. People without a PIN can then only disarm via dashboard buttons (if allowed under PIN rules) or the push button. So: give everyone a PIN (shared PIN allowed) or no one.

rules.title: Trigger rules
rules.description:
{saved}A **trigger rule** triggers only on a **sequence** of sensors – e.g. “front door, then basement within 120 s”. The door alone or the basement alone then trigger nothing.

How a trigger rule works:
- It consists of **steps** that must happen **one after another**. Step 2 only counts once step 1 is fulfilled – and only within the time set at step 1.
- In each step you pick sensors and decide when **this step** is fulfilled: one of them (OR), all of them in any order (AND) or at least N different ones.
- When the last step is fulfilled, there is an alarm – immediately or after the entry delay.

Each alarm profile chooses which trigger rules apply. One fulfilled trigger rule is enough.

**Existing trigger rules:**
{rules}

menu_options.rule_yaml_add: New trigger rule as YAML (expert mode)

rule_delete.title: Delete trigger rule
rule_delete.description: The trigger rule is also removed from all alarm profiles.

rule_meta.title: Trigger rule: name and result
rule_meta.description: Name the trigger rule and decide what happens when all steps are fulfilled. You add the steps one by one afterwards.

data_description.result: “Entry delay” still gives time to disarm (time from the alarm profile), then alarm.

rule_step.title: Step {step}
rule_step.description:
**So far:** {rule_text}

Pick the sensors of this step and when **this step** is fulfilled. The setting only applies to this step. The next step only counts afterwards – that creates the order. Whatever may happen in any order belongs in **one** step with “all of them”.

data.zones: Sensor groups (any sensor of the group)

data_description.within: From the moment this step is fulfilled, the next step has this much time. Irrelevant for the last step. For “all” or “at least N” in the first step also: how close its sensors must be.

triggering.title: Alarm triggering
triggering.description:
{saved}What triggers an alarm?

- **Sensor groups** bundle sensors that belong together (e.g. doors, windows, basement).
- **Trigger rules** only trigger on a sequence of sensors (e.g. “door, then basement”).

In each **alarm profile** you choose which sensor groups trigger alone and which trigger rules apply.

menu_options.zones: Sensor groups – which sensors belong together
menu_options.always_active: Always active – sensors that trigger even when disarmed
menu_options.helper_create: Create a sensor from another sensor (e.g. temperature → frost warning)

rule_unless.title: Not if before …
rule_unless.description:
**So far:** {rule_text}

The trigger rule does **not** apply if one of these sensors triggered within the given time **before step 1** – e.g. someone already moving around inside who then opens a window is no burglar. Affects this trigger rule only. Deselect everything = remove the exception.

data.zones: Sensor groups (any sensor of the group)

rule_yaml.title: Trigger rule as YAML
rule_yaml.description:
Expert mode: the whole trigger rule as YAML. Sensor groups by name (`group: Basement`), sensors by entity ID (`sensor: binary_sensor.x`).

- Steps: `any: [...]` (one of), `all: [...]` (all), `count: 2` + `of: [...]` (at least N), nestable; `within:` time until the next step.
- `result:` alarm, entry_delay or notify (notification only).
- `unless:` expression + `before:` seconds – not if that happened within this time before step 1.
- `conditions:` list: `time` (after/before/weekdays), `person` (entity, in: home/not_home/zone.x), `state` (entity, is), `numeric` (entity, above/below, attribute), `and`/`or`/`not`. Not evaluable = met. Per condition optionally `if_unknown: not_met` = not met when unknown.

Examples are in the documentation.

always_active.title: Always active
always_active.description:
These sensors trigger **even while disarmed** – e.g. safe, gun cabinet, garden shed, panic button.

- **Disarmed:** by default only a critical notification (breaks through Do Not Disturb) and a Home Assistant notification. With “Use sirens” there is an alarm with the chosen sirens; “End alarm” returns to disarmed.
- **Armed:** immediate alarm with the reaction of the active alarm profile.

Hardware release, test mode and fire lock apply as always.

areas.title: Areas
areas.description:
{saved}Areas can be armed **independently** – e.g. the garage while someone is in the house. Names are free.

Each alarm profile belongs to exactly one area (chosen in the alarm profile). Sensor groups and trigger rules can be used in all areas. With two or more areas, each area gets its own panel plus **“All areas”**.

The first area (default “Haus”) is the existing system – it can be renamed but not deleted. Always-active sensors, homecoming observation and the “everyone left” reminder belong to it.

area_delete.title: Delete area
area_delete.description: An area can only be deleted when no alarm profile belongs to it.

area_settings.title: Area: {area}
area_settings.description: The name appears on the panel (“Hauswacht” plus the name) and in notifications.

notify_settings.title: Recipients and events
notify_settings.description: General recipients get every message for which the event has no recipients of its own. Alarm, door opened and alarm ended go to the profile's recipients first. Buttons in notifications only work with the Home Assistant app.

event_alarm_ended.description: Who ended the alarm. Profile recipients first.

event_unconfirmed.name: Unconfirmed trigger
event_unconfirmed.description: A trigger rule was started but not fulfilled in time (e.g. only the door) – there was no alarm. Default: off.

event_unconfirmed_frequent.name: Sensor often triggers alone
event_unconfirmed_frequent.description: The same sensor started a trigger rule three times within an hour that was not fulfilled – a hint to check it. Default: off.

event_rule_notify.name: Trigger rule “notification only”
event_rule_notify.description: A trigger rule with the result “notification only” was fulfilled. Default: on.

event_always_active.name: Always-active sensor
event_always_active.description: An always-active sensor triggered while disarmed (without siren). Critical. Default: on.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: {saved}Push messages to the Home Assistant app and speech output on speakers (e.g. Echo devices).

notify_text_edit.title: Custom text

speech.title: Speech output
speech.description:
Speakers are devices with notify entities, e.g. Echo devices (“Alexa Devices” integration). Announcement or speak is chosen per event.

**Repeat:** the alarm announcement repeats every N seconds until the alarm ends (0 = once).

**Quiet hours:** only events allowed “also during quiet hours” are spoken.

A silent alarm is never spoken, the duress alert never goes to speakers.

speech_event_edit.title: Speech – event
speech_event_edit.description:
Default text: “{default}”
Current preview: “{preview}”

Placeholders: {placeholders}. Empty = default text. With several areas the area name is put in front of the default text.

{error}

zone_types.title: Sensors and their types
zone_types.description:
The type decides **how** a sensor reacts. It is proposed from the device class; only change it if it does not fit (e.g. a window used to enter the house as **Door**).

- **Door:** entry delay, can be an exit door for “arm on close”
- **Window:** instant alarm
- **Motion:** waits during the entry delay, otherwise instant
- **Tamper:** always reported, even disarmed
- **Technical (water, gas, frost …):** always active, even disarmed – never part of arming, notification only by default
- **Other:** instant alarm (to be safe)

helper_create.title: Create a sensor from another sensor
helper_create.description:
Turns a measurement (e.g. temperature, humidity, power) into a sensor: Hauswacht creates a **threshold helper** in Home Assistant (afterwards under Settings → Devices & services → Helpers, editable and deletable there) and uses it right away.

- **Upper limit:** triggers when the value is above
- **Lower limit:** triggers when the value is below
- **Hysteresis:** margin before it counts as normal again – prevents flapping (e.g. 1 for temperature)

Only a new helper is created; nothing existing is changed.

siren_settings.title: Alarm devices – sirens
siren_settings.description:
Register the sirens Hauswacht may use for intrusion alarms. Fire safety: Hauswacht never switches a siren on or off while any smoke detector reports fire, or while the fire state of a registered siren is unknown. Siren control stays LOCKED until you enable it here and confirm.

A siren that only appears as a switch in Home Assistant is easiest turned into a siren with the wizard “Create siren from switch”.

data.confirm_hardware: I confirm: real sirens may sound during an alarm
data.sirens_allow_switch: Experts: allow switches directly as sirens

data_description.sirens_allow_switch: Only needed if you don't want to use the wizard “Create siren from switch”. Hauswacht turns such a switch on in an alarm and off again after the alarm duration – with release, fire lock and test mode like any siren. But Hauswacht cannot know what the device does when switched on: only select pure alarm sirens, never smoke detectors or other devices.

siren_test_next.description:
Pre-check (no sound): {preview}

siren_test_settings.title: Siren test – reminder and pre-warning
siren_test_settings.description:
**Reminder:** reports “siren test due” when a siren has not been (successfully) tested for longer than chosen – at most once a week.

**Pre-warning:** sends a notification “siren test in 10 seconds” to the general recipients before the first sound.

homecoming_signals.title: Homecoming: additional signals per person
homecoming_signals.description:
Further signals per person that can report “home” – observation only, nothing is switched:

- **Wi-Fi sensor** of the companion app (`sensor.…_wifi_connection` or `sensor.…_ssid`): home when connected to a home Wi-Fi
- **Bluetooth** (e.g. Bermuda) or **FRITZ!Box** tracker: `device_tracker.…`
- **Approach** (“Proximity” integration): direction sensor `sensor.…_direction_of_travel` – towards/arrived = home
- **Binary sensors**: on = home

Hauswacht also evaluates the **earliest signal** per person (any source reports home).

controls.title: Control devices
controls.description: {saved}Control devices are keypads, NFC stickers and RFID readers. Identification uses the **users' credentials**: PIN or RFID card/fob (under Users and PINs). Rights, validity, lock after wrong entries and duress PIN apply as on the panel.

control_learn.title: Learning new cards
control_learn.description: An unknown card held to a keypad or reader shows up at the user under “RFID cards/tags” as “new” – but only while **all areas are disarmed**, and only for the time set here. After that it is forgotten and must be read again.

data_description.card_learn_minutes: Minutes (1–60). 0 = learning off; card IDs can then only be typed.

control_keypad.title: Keypad (Zigbee2MQTT)
control_keypad.description:
For alarm keypads following the Zigbee standard (e.g. frient/Develco KEPZB-110/KEYZB-110, Linkind, Centralite, Heiman). Hauswacht receives key, PIN or card and **confirms** each entry (valid, invalid credential, not ready); then the keypad shows the state (delays, armed, alarm). For this Hauswacht sends to `TOPIC/set` – state display only.

The keypad's tamper contact is a separate binary sensor in Home Assistant – add it to a sensor group (type tamper).

data_description.topic: E.g. `zigbee2mqtt/Keypad hall` (base topic + device name in Zigbee2MQTT).
data_description.login: **Card and PIN:** both credentials of the same user within 30 s (the keypad answers the first one with “not ready”).
data_description.emergency: **Silent:** important push message. **Alarm:** also immediate alarm – disarmed with the sirens under “Always active”, armed with those of the active profile.

control_sticker.title: NFC sticker (companion app)
control_sticker.description:
An NFC sticker at the door, scanned with the Home Assistant app. The sticker only says **where and what** – identification is the **phone**: the logged-in Home Assistant account must be linked to an authorized Hauswacht user (Users and PINs → Home Assistant user).

Find the ID under Settings → Areas, labels & zones → Tags (after the first scan).

control_reader.title: RFID/NFC reader
control_reader.description: A fixed reader that fires the “tag scanned” event in Home Assistant (e.g. ESPHome with PN532/RC522). Identification uses the **users' RFID cards** (Users and PINs → RFID cards).

data_description.login: **Card and PIN:** after the card, confirm the same user by PIN at a keypad in the same area within 30 s.

siren_from_switch.title: Create siren from switch
siren_from_switch.description:
Some sirens only appear as a switch (`switch.…`) in Home Assistant. The wizard creates the Home Assistant helper **“Change device type of a switch”** with type **Siren** and adds the new siren to Hauswacht right away. The switch is not switched; Home Assistant hides it and shows the siren instead. To undo: delete the helper under Settings → Devices & services → Helpers.

Only pick real alarm sirens – with a switch Hauswacht cannot tell what the device does when switched on.

data.confirm: I confirm: this is a pure alarm siren, not a smoke detector

siren_tones.title: Tone per siren
siren_tones.description: Normally Hauswacht picks a burglar tone itself (burglar, emergency …). Some sirens have their own tone names – e.g. the Homematic IP alarm siren (HmIP-ASIR): `FREQUENCY_RISING_AND_FALLING`. Set the tone here for such sirens. Which siren?

code.description: Required if a PIN is needed for arming.

simulate_trigger.name: Simulate sensor
simulate_trigger.description: Simulates the triggering of a configured sensor. Only possible in test mode; no device is switched.

sensor.name: Sensor
sensor.description: Configured sensor whose triggering is simulated.

simulate_state.name: Simulate sensor state
simulate_state.description: Makes Hauswacht see a sensor state (open/triggered, closed/idle, unavailable) or resets it to the real value. Test mode only; the device and its state in Home Assistant stay unchanged.

simulate_reset.name: Reset simulation
simulate_reset.description: All simulated sensors back to their real state.

siren_test.name: Siren test
siren_test.description: Sounds ONE siren briefly (real sound, at most 10 s). Only disarmed, with hardware enabled, not in test mode, never during fire; administrators only.

siren_test_result.name: Siren test: result
siren_test_result.description: Stores whether the siren was heard.

reset_code_lock.name: Reset failed attempts
reset_code_lock.description: Resets the counter of wrong PIN/card entries and a running PIN lock. Administrators only.

users_without_pin.title: Hauswacht: not everyone has a PIN
users_without_pin.description:
As soon as a PIN exists, the panel (and Alexa) require it **from everyone** to disarm. These people have no PIN and cannot disarm there: **{people}**.

Options:
- Give them a PIN under Hauswacht → Configure → System settings → Users and PINs (a shared family PIN is allowed), or
- enable “Allow dashboard buttons despite PIN” under PIN rules (currently: {buttons}) – dashboard buttons and the push button then keep working without a PIN.

Scheduled profiles and presence automation are not affected.

check_finding.title: Hauswacht: {hint}
